description: Rotates an incoming 3D vector around the diagonal axis through the origin and the point 1,1,1, which cycles the coordinates into one another

params.text: Sets the twist angle from -3 to +3, one unit per 120 degrees, so each whole unit cycles the coordinates exactly once and 0 leaves the vector as it arrived
Attenuates and inverts the twist CV
Adds a Tricorder to the right, which plots the output vector in 3D

inputs.text: The vector to be rotated, usually a 3-channel polyphonic cable; missing channels count as 0V, channels past the third are ignored, and nothing patched counts as the origin

outputs.text: The rotated vector as a 3-channel polyphonic signal, x on channel 1, y on channel 2 and z on channel 3
The x component of the rotated vector; right-clicking this port inverts its voltage
The y component of the rotated vector; right-clicking this port inverts its voltage
The z component of the rotated vector; right-clicking this port inverts its voltage

menu: Insert Tricorder on right — adds a Tricorder to the right, which plots the outgoing vector in 3D
Flip voltage polarity — on the X, Y or Z output port's own menu, not the panel menu: inverts that port's voltage, which is reflected in the P output and in anything graphing to the right
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero

inputs.1:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±5V.
